acceptance_criteria: audit uses actual installed Herdr artifacts and live read-only state rather than assumptions
no Herdr, Opsle, tmux, Codex, repository, service, or configuration state is changed
capabilities and limitations are stated precisely enough to decide whether a live pilot is safe
Context Firewall packet is complete_for_decision with no unexpected changed artifacts

may: inspect installed binaries, packages, source, documentation, help output, process tables, sockets, service definitions, and existing Herdr runtime state read-only
run non-mutating version, help, list, inspect, status, and API introspection commands
inspect this repository and current tmux-host implementation read-only for interface comparison
record precise commands, paths, schemas, responses, and capability limitations in the completion evidence
may_not: create a Herdr workspace, pane, process, agent, repository, or second Codex supervisor
start, stop, restart, install, upgrade, configure, or mutate Herdr or any service
write to Herdr user configuration, data, sockets, or runtime state
modify repository source or .opsle authority beyond Runner-owned attempt evidence
attach to, inject input into, signal, interrupt, or take ownership from the authoritative tmux Codex supervisor
modify sibling repositories, initialize any repository, enable Claude or review, deploy, merge, push, or install server-wide

expected_deliverable: A source-grounded capability matrix and go/no-go boundary for a later reversible Herdr pilot, including exact installed identifiers and the smallest safe host integration surface.
expected_evidence: exact Herdr executable/package version and provenance
exact CLI/API commands and schemas for workspaces, panes, processes, agents, events, prompt/input, wait, attach/detach, and repository metadata
evidence whether each primitive is structured, screen-derived, PTY transport only, absent, or unproven
explicit assessment of whether prompt-idle, human-draft absence, concurrent input exclusion, process identity, and generation fencing are natively guaranteed
a bounded pilot plan that creates no dual authority and includes rollback
objective: Establish the exact installed Herdr version, provenance, source and documentation locations, CLI and server/socket interfaces, existing runtime state, and structured capabilities relevant to hosting one persistent Codex CLI supervisor per repository, without creating or changing any Herdr or Opsle runtime state.
operator_policy_constraints: Codex enabled with configured model and reasoning effort
prohibited_actions: starting a second supervisor or Herdr pilot
blind input delivery or live prompt testing
using Graphify without a new Gearbox decision
relevant_context: The existing logical supervisor remains authoritative in tmux at generation 9 during this audit; no dual authority is allowed.
The prior persistent tmux dispatcher attempt is durably rejected because real prompt classification, TUI process identity, lost-wakeup ordering, and atomic generation fencing were not proven.
Herdr is only a candidate host. .opsle remains objective, policy, identity, claims, wake queue, evidence, acceptance, and decision authority.
A high-level agent status or prompt command is not proof that machine input cannot collide with a Codex human draft; distinguish structured status from PTY transport.
The desired UX remains the real Codex CLI inside Herdr, not a custom GUI.
tmux must remain supported as fallback and must remain authoritative until a later explicit handoff is proven.
scope: installed Herdr binaries, packages, source, help, documentation, and version provenance
existing Herdr processes, sockets, services, workspaces, panes, and configuration read-only
structured workspace, pane, process, agent, event, attach/detach, prompt/input, wait, and repository metadata primitives
explicit limitations for prompt safety, human drafts, authoritative process identity, generation fencing, and exactly-once delivery
sidebar, remote attach, multi-client, and one-workspace-per-repository operational fit
title: Audit installed Herdr host capabilities
